title: WhatToLookAt: learned relations become a sensing budget
summary: WhatToLookAt takes the history-written relation machinery from SighImageFactorization and asks a compressed-sensing-style engineering question: if experience has already learned useful structure, how many future physical observations can be omitted? Gate 0 establishes an oracle upper bound, Gate 1 earns the relation from ordered common-fate history and spends it on a spatially rearranged future, and Gate 2 turns local correspondence confidence into a local sensing budget. The branch keeps the Sigh/Sihti operator framing but changes the currency from segmentation or relation authority to the minimum measurement cost required to maintain reconstruction quality.

nodes.claim: Learns persistent relations from past temporal structure and uses them as a prior for future sparse sensing; local relation uncertainty withdraws sharing authority and purchases extra measurements only where confidence is low.
nodes.survived: A correct relation partition can replace measurements in a piecewise-constant world; common-fate history can learn that partition before a rearranged future is undersampled; confidence-adaptive sensing stays near the oracle cost curve while blind trust and shuffled-confidence controls fail.
nodes.killed: A spatial lattice, a size-matched shuffled relation graph, time-shuffled motion history, and absolute-coordinate memory do not recover the same measurement savings; spending the same number of extra measurements at the wrong uncertain locations does not rescue reconstruction.

edges.why: WhatToLookAt explicitly states that it pushes the compressed-sensing question into the SighImageFactorization/Sihti lineage and operationalizes SighImageFactorization's learned relation state as a prior that can reduce future sensing.

WhatToLookAt explicitly names Sihti in its lineage and carries forward the operator-dependent-structure framing, but does not claim Sihti code inheritance; the new currency is measurement cost rather than residue location.
